events.headline: Russia Launches Massive Missile-Drone Barrage on Kyiv, Killing at Least Seven
events.summary: Russia launched a large combined missile and drone attack (including Zircon/Onyx missiles, Iskander-M and roughly 188 drones) on Kyiv and its region overnight Sept 29-30, striking energy infrastructure and residential areas. The death toll rose to at least seven, including a 14-year-old, with a child killed in rubble in Vyshhorod; it follows a separate Sept 29 strike on Kyiv's Academy of Sciences that killed two.

events.headline: Houthi Forces Seize Yemen's Entire Red Sea Coast, Including Bab al-Mandab Strait
events.summary: Fighting escalated sharply since the early-September Houthi offensive, with government forces conducting air and ground operations across five Taiz locations in 24 hours and more than 146,000 people displaced since July. Saudi warplanes launched 129 air raids in 48 hours across Taiz, Marib, Hodeidah, al-Jawf, Saada, Amran and Hajjah, while Houthi forces reportedly seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline including the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

events.headline: Venezuela's Bolivar Keeps Sliding Even as US-Venezuela Diplomacy Warms
events.summary: Venezuela's bolivar continued weakening to 857.01 per dollar, from 301.37 at the start of 2026, even after acting President Delcy Rodriguez met Trump at the UN General Assembly on Sept 22 in a first such meeting as part of a broader normalization push. No formal deal resulted, and August inflation stood at 8.9%.

events.headline: UN Security Council Extends Haiti Gang Suppression Force Mandate to March 2027
events.summary: The UN Security Council voted 12-0-3 (China, Russia, Pakistan abstaining) on Sept 29 to extend the Gang Suppression Force mandate to March 31, 2027, to help Haitian authorities counter gang violence ahead of December elections. The move follows the deadly Kenscoff massacre and continued gang expansion around Port-au-Prince.

events.headline: ECB's Lagarde and Largest Eurozone Economies Warn on Inflation, Keep October Hike Alive
events.summary: Since euro-area inflation hit 3.3% in August, the ECB raised its deposit rate 25bp to 2.5% on Sept 10. On Sept 28-29 Lagarde and officials from the four largest euro economies warned inflation, already above 3% and possibly reaching about 4% by year-end, has not yet produced dangerous second-round effects, keeping an October rate hike plausible.

events.headline: IDF Kills Hamas Northern Gaza Brigade Commander in Gaza City Strike
events.summary: Israel killed Izz al-Din al-Bik, commander of Hamas's Northern Gaza Brigade, in an airstrike on an apartment building in Gaza City's al-Nasr neighborhood, which Hamas confirmed. He is the third Hamas brigade commander killed in weeks, after commanders in Rafah on Sept 15 and Khan Younis on Sept 11, reportedly located via intelligence from a captured Hamas official.

events.headline: Copilot Stabs Captain Aboard Israel-Bound Flydubai Flight; Passengers Subdue Attacker
events.summary: A cockpit altercation aboard Flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, carrying mostly Israeli passengers, caused the aircraft to plunge about 14,125 feet in 29 seconds before passengers stormed the cockpit and subdued the attacker. The plane diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia; both pilots were hospitalized and Netanyahu called it an apparent attempt to crash the plane.

events.headline: Cuba's Power Grid Suffers Seventh Nationwide Collapse of 2026 Amid US Fuel Blockade
events.summary: Cuba's electrical grid collapsed nationwide on Sept 18 after a high-voltage transmission failure, the island's seventh total collapse of 2026, worsened by a tightened US energy blockade in place since January. The blackout left much of the island in darkness for an extended period.

events.headline: Ethiopia's Army Chief Accuses Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of Backing Tigray Rebels
events.summary: Field Marshal Birhanu Jula publicly accused Eritrea of financing the TPLF and implicated Sudan and Egypt without evidence, amid renewed fighting in which rebels captured strategic northern towns. The claims raise fears of a wider regional conflict; Eritrea denies involvement.

events.headline: French High School Protests Over School Conditions Turn Violent; 440 Detained
events.summary: Protests over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and heat-damaged buildings spread across France, with some incidents turning violent including burned bins and acid thrown at police in seven cases. The interior ministry reported 440 detentions, mostly minors, and 48 injured officers, coinciding with a public-sector pay strike ahead of the 2027 budget.
events.locationName: Nationwide France (Paris, Lille, Marseille, Bordeaux, Lyon)

events.headline: Brazil Supreme Court Rift Deepens Ahead of Oct 4 Election as Polls Show Tied Runoff
events.summary: A week-long public dispute among Brazilian Supreme Court justices Alexandre de Moraes and Andre Mendonca, including canceled sessions and mutual overruling amid graft/bias allegations, has spilled into the presidential race weeks before the Oct 4 vote. Polls show Flavio Bolsonaro erasing Lula's lead in a hypothetical runoff.

events.headline: Sudan's Army Resumes Airstrikes on RSF-Held Nyala, Shoots Down Drone in North Kordofan
events.summary: Sudan's army resumed heavy airstrikes on RSF-held Nyala on Sept 22 after months of calm, hitting ammunition depots and training sites, with further strikes on Sept 27. The army also shot down an RSF-operated Chinese FH-95 drone in North Kordofan, part of roughly eight drones intercepted region-wide over ten days, as the broader Sudan drone war escalates beyond El Obeid.

events.headline: Hurricane Polo Floods Kill Two Children in Jalisco, Mexico; Three Still Missing
events.summary: Hurricane Polo, one of the strongest storms on record for the region, made landfall in Baja California Sur before weakening over mainland Mexico. In Talpa de Allende, Jalisco, flash flooding swept away a home, killing two children aged 3 and 12, with their parents and a tourist still missing; Baja California Sur reported no fatalities despite direct landfall.

events.headline: Russian Drones Repeatedly Cross Into Moldovan and Romanian Airspace
events.summary: Drones, including 'Gerbera'-type, entered Moldovan and Romanian airspace repeatedly around Sept 24, prompting Moldovan airspace closures, Romanian F-16 scrambles and Polish air-defense activation. A fresh drone crashed and exploded near Hirbovat, Moldova on Sept 30, with President Sandu citing 39 airspace violations in 2026 versus 17 in 2025.

events.headline: Argentina's Poverty Rate Jumps to 32.3% in First Half of 2026, Setback for Milei
events.summary: Argentina's statistics agency INDEC reported poverty at 32.3% in H1 2026, up from 28.2%, as basic-basket costs rose about 20% versus 11.5% income growth. Extreme poverty rose to 7.5%, deepening political pressure on President Javier Milei's austerity program.

events.headline: UK PM Andy Burnham Opens Door to Rejoining the EU
events.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the Labour government could go 'all the way' toward EU membership, including single market or customs union options, the first time a UK PM has floated rejoining since the Brexit referendum. He plans to chart a new EU relationship path at a summit later this year.

events.headline: Iran's Rial Hits New Record Low of About 2.5 Million per Dollar
events.summary: Iran's rial fell to a record low of over 2.5 million per US dollar, just 27 days after its previous record of 2.2 million on Sept 2. The slide reflects economic erosion from the ongoing war since late February, a US naval blockade on Iranian oil exports, and expanded sanctions.

events.headline: South Africa: 12 Women's Bodies Found Near Johannesburg, Fueling Serial-Killer Fears
events.summary: Police confirmed 12 women's bodies have been found in Ekurhuleni since mid-July, raising fears of a serial killer, though some cases appear unrelated and arrests have been made in three. President Ramaphosa ordered police to leave 'no stone unturned' in the investigation.

events.headline: Malaysia Begins Mass Deportation of Myanmar Nationals Despite UN Warnings
events.summary: Malaysia deported about 1,500 Myanmar nationals, including children, from Lumut on Sept 29, the first phase of a program that could return up to 5,000 people. The UNHCR expressed concern on Sept 30 given ongoing civil war conditions in Myanmar, though Malaysia says the program is voluntary.

events.headline: DRC Fighting Expands to Masisi/Walikale as M23 Repels Government Offensive
events.summary: Beyond the Fizi/Uvira front in South Kivu, Congolese army and Wazalendo forces launched an offensive toward Ngungu in southern Masisi, North Kivu, but M23 counterattacked and retained territory around Katoyi, Ngululu and Mitimingi. Congo's army accused M23 and Rwanda of ceasefire violations in Masisi/Walikale on Sept 22 despite the Doha roadmap, with continued clashes also reported in Minembwe.

events.headline: South Africa Anti-Immigrant Movement Holds Nationwide Deportation Protests
events.summary: The 'March and March' anti-immigration movement, behind an earlier Sept 3 clash at a Durban-area refugee camp, escalated to a second nationwide day of action on Sept 30 with marches in Pretoria, Johannesburg, Durban and Cape Town demanding undocumented immigrants leave. The group has no legal authority to enforce this; refugee groups fear renewed violence and President Ramaphosa called for calm.

events.headline: South Korea Blames North Korea for DMZ Landmine Blasts, Demands Apology
events.summary: Two blasts on Sept 21 inside the DMZ wounded three South Korean soldiers; the military and UN Command concluded a deliberately planted North Korean anti-personnel mine was responsible, calling it an Armistice violation. Seoul is demanding an apology while Pyongyang denies responsibility.

events.headline: Spain Announces Eviction Ban Through 2030 After Forced Removal of 87-Year-Old Sparks Protests
events.summary: The forcible eviction of 87-year-old Maria del Carmen Abascal from her Madrid home after an unaffordable rent hike sparked large protests. The governing Socialists and Sumar agreed new housing measures including an eviction ban through 2030, rental contract rollover to 2028, and a ban on 'vulture funds'; Abascal has since accepted an offer to return home.

events.headline: Kenya: Dangote and Ruto Break Ground on $16 Billion Lamu Refinery
events.summary: Aliko Dangote and President William Ruto broke ground on a $16 billion, 700,000 barrel-per-day oil refinery in Lamu, described as the largest industrial project in East African history. Construction begins Nov 1, 2026, targeting completion by 2030 and roughly 60,000 jobs.

events.headline: North Korea Tests New 'Hwasongpho-11Ma-1' Hypersonic Missile
events.summary: North Korea test-fired an upgraded Hwasongpho-11Ma-1 short-range hypersonic glide vehicle missile on Sept 20, which reportedly flew 908km and reached 35.8km altitude at about 4,800mph. Kim Jong Un observed the launch with his daughter and called it an 'incurable headache' for adversaries, signaling a move toward operational deployment.
events.locationName: Anbyon County, near Wonsan, North Korea

events.headline: Ecuador Declares 60-Day State of Exception in Eight Provinces to Fight Organized Crime
events.summary: President Daniel Noboa signed Decree 498 declaring a 60-day state of exception across eight provinces, suspending home-inviolability protections, amid persistently high homicide levels tied to organized crime and drug trafficking.

events.headline: Bangladesh Dengue Death Toll Reaches 239 in 2026 as September Sees Worst Monthly Toll
events.summary: Bangladesh's cumulative 2026 dengue death toll has risen to 239, up from 176 in mid-September, with September alone recording 87 deaths, the highest monthly toll of the year. More than 77,600 people have been hospitalized since Jan 1, according to health ministry data.

events.headline: Australia's Central Bank Raises Cash Rate to 4.60%, a 15-Year High
events.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate target 25 basis points to 4.60%, the highest since 2011, citing materializing upside inflation risks with inflation currently at 3.5%, above target. It is the fourth hike of 2026 and adds about $427 per month to the average mortgage repayment.

events.headline: Russian Strikes Across Dnipropetrovsk Region Kill Six, Injure 28
events.summary: A Russian drone and missile strike hit an office building in downtown Dnipro, killing three people including a child and injuring up to 18, while three more were killed in Synelnykove district. The broader Dnipropetrovsk region was struck nearly 30 times.

events.headline: 46 Moldovan MPs File Motion to Suspend President Sandu; Passage Unlikely
events.summary: Opposition MPs filed a motion accusing President Maia Sandu of violating the separation of powers, but suspension requires 67 of 101 votes versus the 46 signatures obtained, making passage unlikely. The presidency called the move Moscow-aligned; a Russian drone crash in Moldova the next morning was noted as a possible related pressure tactic.

events.headline: EU Drafts Individualized Accession Roadmaps for Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro and Albania
events.summary: The European Commission is preparing candidate-specific roadmaps with deadlines and benchmarks for Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro and Albania. Montenegro is furthest along with a target of end-2026, Albania is targeted for 2027, and Ukraine and Moldova for 2028.

events.headline: Indonesia Suspends Officials Over Luxury 'VIP' Prison Cells Near Jakarta
events.summary: Indonesia suspended five officials, including the prison chief, after Ombudsman investigators found more than 10 unauthorized residential units at Cibinong Prison equipped with air conditioning, TVs, a gym and a golf simulator, allegedly used by inmates. The buildings were officially designated as staff housing, and a bribery investigation is ongoing.

events.headline: Colombia's Central Bank Holds Benchmark Rate at 12% in Split Vote
events.summary: Banco de la Republica held its policy rate at 12% for a second consecutive meeting in a reported 4-3 split board vote, amid inflation of 6.24% in August and a weak peso. Policymakers remain divided over the pace of future moves.

events.headline: 13-Year-Old Kills Teacher, Wounds Two in Slovak School Stabbing
events.summary: A 13-year-old student fatally stabbed a 61-year-old teacher and seriously wounded another teacher and a schoolgirl in a village near the Czech border on Sept 29. The suspect was arrested and an organized-crime unit is investigating it as premeditated murder.

events.headline: M5.9 Earthquake Strikes Off Taiwan's Eastern Coast Near Hualien
events.summary: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake, per Taiwan's Central Weather Administration, struck offshore about 136km east of Hualien County at roughly 13.3km depth on Sept 30. Intensity of 2 was felt in five counties with no damage or injuries reported, though officials warn of possible aftershocks over the next 3-5 days.

events.headline: Thailand-Cambodia Border Ceasefire Remains Fragile Amid Sporadic Incursions
events.summary: Despite the December 2025 ceasefire and ASEAN observer monitoring, Thailand and Cambodia continue trading accusations over incidents such as Cambodian trench-digging near Chong Sa-Ngam on Sept 14 and alleged Cambodian military use of the Preah Vihear World Heritage area on Sept 12. No major clashes or casualties were reported in September, continuing the chronic dispute.

events.headline: Hurricane Polo Remnants Trigger Flash Floods, Near-Collapse of New Mexico Dam
events.summary: Remnants of Hurricane Polo produced flash flooding that pushed New Mexico's McLeod Dam toward failure, prompting evacuations in Rincon, Salem, Garfield, Hatch and Placitas. Most evacuation orders were lifted by Sept 30, with Rincon remaining under order.

events.headline: Japan's Extraordinary Diet Session to Convene Oct 5 Over Tax-Cut Bill
events.summary: An extraordinary Diet session convenes Oct 5 and is expected to run about 69 days, with PM Sanae Takaichi pushing a temporary cut of the food consumption tax from 8% to 1% for two years plus electoral reform reducing Lower House seats. Passage is uncertain since the ruling coalition lacks an Upper House majority.

events.headline: China's Factory Activity Returns to Growth in September
events.summary: China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 in September from 49.8, ending two months of contraction, while the private RatingDog PMI rose to 52.1. The improvement offers some relief amid ongoing trade and economic pressures.

events.headline: Peru's Congress to Vote on Censuring Interior Minister Over Security Crisis
events.summary: Thirty-five opposition deputies filed a censure motion against Interior Minister Cesar Astudillo Salcedo citing 'manifest incapacity' amid record homicides (1,499 through August) and the killing of journalist Susy Aponte. The motion needs 66 of 130 votes to pass.

events.headline: Typhoon Surigae Nears Japan's Izu Islands With Strong Winds and Heavy Rain
events.summary: Typhoon Surigae, near peak intensity with 90-knot winds, is tracking past the Daito Islands toward south of Honshu and is expected to skirt Japan's Izu Islands around Oct 1. Interaction with an autumn rain front is expected to intensify winds, high waves and heavy rain along Japan's eastern Pacific coast.

events.headline: Lebanon Blast in Nabatieh al-Fawqa Wounds Four; Initially Misattributed to Israel
events.summary: Lebanon's army initially reported that an Israeli strike wounded a soldier and three civilians while troops escorted residents inspecting properties. A subsequent inspection determined the blast was caused by an unexploded or suspicious object rather than an Israeli strike.

events.headline: West Nile Virus and Chikungunya Cases Continue Seasonal Rise in France; Kosovo Reports First Cases
events.summary: As of Sept 21, France had recorded 117 autochthonous West Nile virus cases across seven regions and three chikungunya outbreaks (25 cases) in Tarn and Gironde. Kosovo reported its first two locally-acquired West Nile cases in 2026 as of Sept 23, part of routine seasonal surveillance rather than an acute outbreak.
